briefings.title: Satya Nadella on Open vs Closed Models: Who Wins | Why Companies Need to Own Their Own Intelligence
briefings.tldr: Satya Nadella argues that because AI alignment cannot be solved solely through scaling, enterprises must adopt a "zero trust" containment architecture and own their intelligence via private evaluation benchmarks.

briefings.title: Nikesh Arora on The Future of Token Costs | Memory Becoming the Moat & Why Enterprise AI Isn't Ready

people.name: Nikesh Arora
people.role: Chairman and CEO, Palo Alto Networks

briefings.tldr: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora predicts that token costs will plummet to one-tenth of current pricing within three to five years, driving a massive wave of G&A headcount reduction as opinionated AI applications replace traditional SaaS workflows.

briefings.title: Flexport CEO: Why Revenge and Patriotism are the Best Founder Traits
briefings.tldr: Flexport is on track to hit $450 million in net revenue and break even this year, with plans to IPO once it reaches substantial EBITDA profitability.

briefings.title: Andrej Karpathy Joins Anthropic | SpaceX Files S1: How Does it Trade | Cerebras Smashes Day 1
briefings.tldr: As elite AI firms like Anthropic and OpenAI command staggering private valuations and push compute grants directly to startups, legacy SaaS companies face a structural squeeze, compounded by a looming public and political backlash over AI-driven white-collar layoffs.

briefings.title: Demis Hassabis: Why AGI is Bigger than the Industrial Revolution & Where Are The Bottlenecks in AI
briefings.tldr: Demis Hassabis (Co-Founder & CEO of Google DeepMind) predicts AGI—defined as a system matching all human cognitive capabilities—will likely arrive within the next five years, ushering in a shift ten times the magnitude and speed of the Industrial Revolution.

briefings.title: Marc Andreessen: Will a16z Go Public & Why Labour Displacement with AI is Wrong?

people.name: Marc Andreessen
people.role: Co-Founder and General Partner, Andreessen Horowitz

briefings.tldr: Marc Andreessen argues that the narrative of AI-driven labor displacement is fundamentally incorrect, asserting instead that current tech layoffs are a correction for massive corporate overstaffing.

briefings.title: a16z, Anish Acharya: Is SaaS Dead in a World of AI? | Who Wins the Dev Market: Cursor or Claude Code
briefings.tldr: Contrary to the "SaaS-pocalypse" narrative, AI is not killing software but expanding its reach into the 90% of enterprise spend currently untouched by automation, while simultaneously shifting the industry from a "hostage" model of high switching costs to one based on outcome-driven value and proprietary data moats.
